help.concept: A nested list should be contained by the list item it describes.
help.hint_1: Ask which element owns the subtopics.
help.hint_2: Keep the child list inside the parent li.

nested-quiz-multi.title: Recognize useful nested-list patterns
nested-quiz-multi.prompt: Which two examples naturally call for nested lists?

help.concept: Nested lists are useful for meaningful subgroups.
help.hint_2: Flat prose and metadata do not need nested lists.

options.a: A course area with lessons grouped underneath it
options.b: A single paragraph of biography text
options.c: A club with project categories and projects under each category
options.d: A page title in the browser tab

help.concept: The child ul belongs inside the Robotics li.

nested-quiz-blank.prompt: Fill the one blank with the list container that makes two unordered subtopics under Robotics.

help.concept: A nested unordered list is a ul inside the parent li.
help.hint_1: The blank is already inside Robotics.
help.hint_2: Choose the ul containing two li elements.

nest-inside-item.title: Nest a child list inside its parent list item
nest-inside-item.bodyMarkdown:
Nested lists describe hierarchy. Put the child list inside the `
  • ` that owns it. ```html
    • Robotics
      • Sensors
      • Programming
    ``` Sensors and Programming belong specifically to Robotics. Break the nested example down line by line: the outer `
      ` begins the main list, then `
    • Robotics` begins the parent item. Before that parent item closes, a second `
        ` begins its child list. Sensors and Programming are child `
      • ` elements. After the inner `
      ` closes, the parent `
      • ` closes, preserving the parent-child relationship.

mix-list-meaning.title: Choose the child list type from its own meaning
mix-list-meaning.bodyMarkdown:
A nested list does not have to use the same type as its parent. A parent `<ul>` can contain an `<ol>` when the child items are steps.

The outer list answers “which groups?” while the inner list can answer “in what order?”

readable-hierarchy.title: Close each nested structure where it belongs
readable-hierarchy.bodyMarkdown:
Indentation helps humans see nesting even though the browser follows the element structure. Keep a child list inside its parent `<li>`, then close the parent item before moving to its sibling.

Clear nesting makes complex content easier to read and debug.
